items.topic: 原生交易断言：签名之外的结果约束
items.title: EF 博客：原生交易断言如何约束交易的最终结果
items.note: 文章区分两类失败：意图不符（Bybit、BadgerDAO，被篡改的前端给出与用户以为的不同的签名请求）和结果不符（Aave 与 CoW 的抵押品互换，用户约 5,040 万美元的 aEthUSDT 换到约 3.6 万美元的代币）。共同问题是缺少一条独立于交易构造者、在执行中强制的结果规则。以太坊目前没有通用机制让链上代码检查一笔交易产生的全部净状态变化和事件，EIP-7906 是一种可能方案，与 Clear Signing 配合。
items.title_en: EF Blog: how native transaction assertions could enforce a transaction's final outcome
items.note_en: . The post separates two failure modes. In an intent mismatch (Bybit, BadgerDAO), a compromised frontend supplied a signing request that differed from what users believed they were approving. In an outcome mismatch (the Aave and CoW collateral swap), a user swapped about $50.4 million of aEthUSDT and received tokens worth about $36,000. What all cases lacked was a rule over the resulting state, defined independently of the transaction builder and enforced during execution. Ethereum has no general mechanism for onchain code to inspect all the net state changes and events a transaction produces; EIP-7906 is one possible approach, alongside Clear Signing.

summary_en: The EF's Trillion Dollar Security initiative published a post proposing native transaction assertions to enforce a transaction's final outcome, with EIP-7906 as one candidate design. Frame transactions kept growing: EIP-8141 adds a set-delegation frame for codeless senders, and EIP-8250 lets a transaction scope its nonce keys to the payer. L2BEAT's Luca Donno ran a half-mocked native rollup on a devnet based on frames-devnet-0.
